text.text: The town council meets about the pothole on Elm Street. It's been there eleven years and has its own fan page. Half the room recognises you from the fountain video.
The town council meets about the pothole on Elm Street. It's been there eleven years. It has its own fan page and a small fish.

choices.label: Stand up and give a fiery speech

ok.text: “Fill. The. Hole.” The room chants it. The pothole is filled by Friday. They name the tarmac after you.

effects.remember: Got the Elm Street pothole fixed with one fiery speech.

fail.text: You shout so hard you knock over the council's water jug. The pothole is now a listed monument.

choices.label: Calmly present a petition with 400 signatures

ok.text: The council has never seen a petition before. They're scared. The hole is filled.

effects.remember: Got the pothole fixed with a 400-name petition.

fail.text: You start calm. Then the councillor calls the pothole “character”. You call him things.

hothead.text: You get to signature number three before you flip the table. The pothole fish watches you get escorted out.

choices.label: Find out what {rival} thinks and take the opposite side

ok.text: {rival} wants to keep the pothole “as heritage”. You win the room by promising tarmac. {rival} sulks.

fail.text: {rival} wanted the hole filled. You argued for keeping it. You are now the pothole person.

choices.label: Point out the council has been paying a company to fill it every year since 2015

ok.text: There is a scandal, an investigation and a new pothole contract. Guess who's on the committee.

effects.remember: Found eleven years of pothole fraud in the small print.

choices.label: Bring your class to present a project about the pothole

ok.text: Thirty eight-year-olds in hi-vis jackets. The council never stood a chance.

effects.remember: Sent thirty kids to defeat the town council.

choices.label: Live-blog the meeting for the Gazette

ok.text: Your live blog gets more readers than the Gazette's horoscope. The hole is filled out of shame.

effects.remember: Live-blogged the pothole meeting into history.

text.text: People keep stopping you in the street to thank you for the pothole. A man in a suit says you should run for council. Then for mayor.
A man in a suit says the town needs “a fresh face” at the next election. He looks at your face. He shrugs. “Fresh enough.”

choices.label: Launch your campaign in the town square

ok.text: Forty people come. Twelve stay. One brings a banner with your name spelled right. It's a movement.

effects.remember: Launched your campaign for mayor in the town square.

fail.text: It rains. Four people come. Two are your mum. The other two were waiting for a bus.

effects.remember: Launched your campaign to four people in the rain.

ok.text: {friend} prints 5,000 leaflets with your face on them. Your face is everywhere. It's working.

effects.remember: {friend} ran your campaign. Your face was on every lamppost.

cast.did: covered the town in your face

fail.text: {friend} prints 5,000 leaflets. The slogan is “Vote for me, I guess”. {Friend.he} thought it was funny.

choices.label: Knock on every door in town

ok.text: You knock on 3,000 doors. You drink 3,000 cups of tea. People remember you. Your bladder remembers you.

effects.remember: Knocked on every door in town for your campaign.

fail.text: You knock on four doors and go home for a nap. The nap is great. The campaign isn't.

lazy.text: You knock on one door. It's your own. You let yourself in and lie down. The campaign is “paused”.

title: The Town Fair
text: You've been asked to judge the pie contest at the town fair. There are nine pies. One is {rival}'s mum's. One is {crush}'s. One is clearly from a shop.

ok.text: The shop pie wins. It was the best. The town respects your honesty and nobody speaks to you for a month.

effects.remember: Judged the pie contest fairly. The shop pie won.

ok.text: {crush} is thrilled. The town notices. There are whispers. Lovely whispers.

effects.remember: Gave {crush}'s pie first prize. Everyone noticed.

fail.text: {crush} is mortified. {Crush.he} bought the pie in a shop. It was the shop pie.

choices.label: Give it to {rival}'s mum's pie, to make peace

ok.text: {rival}'s mum hugs you. {rival} looks at you like you're a stranger, then nods once. It's a start.
